# Creative — Jordan

## Where things stand

Coda — the practice-tracking app Jordan's been building for musicians — is no longer a side project in the "someday portfolio piece" sense. As of September 9th it's the centerpiece of the Northlight application, and as of the 11th, Ana (who runs design there) singled it out specifically, including the part where Jordan got it wrong. Jordan has an onsite coming up in the next week or so. Meanwhile Jordan is three days out from Dev's gig (Sept 19) and has signed up for a second open mic, at the Fern on September 27th.

## How it got here

Coda started as something Jordan tinkered with at Groundwork, the coffee shop that became the reliable setting for almost every creative session logged here — practice log screens, a pulsing-circle metronome, quick-start cards. By late July it was already doing double duty as therapy: Mika named this out loud on 7/31 ("maybe Coda IS the portfolio update"), and the pattern repeated for months — bad day at work, spiral, then Groundwork, then two hours of building, then feeling human again. Jordan noticed the cycle explicitly on 8/12 and again after the reorg landed on 9/1, when the spiral shrank from a full day to twenty minutes on the couch before getting up and going to build.

Dev's arrival mattered structurally, not just personally. Meeting on 8/8, then dinner on 8/15 where Dev asked for a "free play" mode for unstructured practice — that became the feature that made Coda real. The breakthrough came 8/25 (the timestamp-marker idea). Then on 9/3, Dev actually used it and broke it open in a different way: Jordan had built a "trophy case" for marking good moments, and Dev used the same feature as a bug tracker, marking everything that went wrong. Jordan sat with that discomfort for twelve days before rebuilding the review screen on 9/15 — stripping out "highlights" language entirely, making marks neutral until named. That fix, and the honesty about not seeing the problem for nine days of daily use, became the strongest part of the Northlight case study.

Music as performance runs alongside the coding thread. Mika signed Jordan up for the open mic at The Lantern without much warning; Jordan practiced "Fast Car" with Pepper howling along on 8/17, then performed it shakily but real on 8/21, with Dev and Mika both there. That night knit the three of them together. Dad's old picks showed up on 9/16, handed off to Dev for the gig — a small, unplanned handoff that landed harder than expected.

## Open threads

The Northlight onsite is still ahead — full day, four interviews, portfolio presentation. Dev's gig is the 19th, tonight by this document's date. The Fern open mic is the 27th. Coda itself has no ending yet: no launch, no users beyond Dev, no verdict on whether the recommendation-engine question from 8/18 ever gets resolved. And underneath all of it, the move to legacy marketing under Priya starts the 21st regardless of what happens with Northlight — the two timelines are running at each other and Jordan hasn't said yet what happens if the job offer doesn't come through before that date arrives.
